title: Build a Minimal Prompt Template Engine
summary: Render {{variable}}-style prompt templates and raise a clear error when a required variable is missing.
description:
## Scenario

Most prompt-engineering codebases eventually grow a small templating layer: a prompt is written once with placeholders, and filled in with different values per request. A silent typo in a variable name (or a caller forgetting to pass one) should fail loudly — not silently send a broken prompt to an expensive LLM call.

## Task

Implement in `solution.py`:

- `render_template(template: str, variables: dict[str, str]) -> str` — replaces every `{{name}}` placeholder in `template` with `variables["name"]`.
- If the template references a variable that isn't in `variables`, raise `ValueError` with a message that includes the missing variable's name.

## Requirements

- Placeholders may have surrounding whitespace: `{{ name }}` and `{{name}}` both work.
- A variable passed in `variables` but never referenced in the template is simply ignored — not an error.
- The same variable may appear more than once in the template.
- A template with no placeholders is returned unchanged.
